amendments.rule: The definite direct-object marker `אֵת` (H853) has no English realization of its own and is normally its own `unrepresented` unit; that is the ruling on the large majority of its occurrences. It takes English only where the ASV spends a word on the object relation itself and no other morpheme licenses that word. Four families qualify. An English verb may reach its object through a preposition — *hearken unto*, *spake unto*, *inquire of*, *fight against*, *send for* — where that preposition exists only to attach the object to the verb; it is the marker's rendering, not the object noun's, and the marker heads on it. An appositional or resumptive marker may be rendered *even* or *to wit*. **But only a marker standing on the very phrase that English word introduces.** Where the ASV writes an appositional *even* or *to wit* before a phrase no marker marks, no morpheme licenses it and it is its own `added` unit under rule 30, whatever markers stand elsewhere in the clause: `וְחַקּוֹתָ עָלֶיהָ עִיר אֵת־יְרוּשָׁלִָם` → *portray upon it a city,* ***even*** *Jerusalem* gives *even* to the marker, which stands on the appositive itself, while `נָתַתִּי לְךָ אֵת־שְׁנֵי עֲוֺנָם לְמִסְפַר יָמִים שְׁלֹשׁ־מֵאוֹת וְתִשְׁעִים יוֹם` → *a number of days,* ***even*** *three hundred and ninety days* leaves the *even* `added`, because the clause's one marker stands on `שְׁנֵי עֲוֺנָם`, which the ASV renders bare. Do not reach across the clause for a marker to carry such a word, for the reason rule 42 gives about a surplus *and*: the word is written beside those renderings rather than inside one of them. **But an *even* the ASV writes inside another morpheme's own multi-word rendering is not an appositional *even* at all, and the preceding sentence does not reach it.** Where the ASV expands an extent or limit preposition as *even unto*, *even to*, *even till* or *even for*, the whole expression is that preposition's rendering and belongs to its unit, headed by rule 24 on the word carrying the relation — *unto*, *to*, *till*, *for* — and the *even* is neither `added` nor any marker's, whatever markers stand elsewhere in the clause: `וַיִּירַשׁ אֶת־אַרְצוֹ מֵאַרְנֹן עַד־יַבֹּק עַד־בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן` → *from the Arnon unto the Jabbok* ***even unto*** *the children of Ammon* gives *even unto* to the second `עַד`, which is the morpheme the two words are written for. Read what the English word stands before, which is this rule's subtraction test again: an appositional *even* stands before a nominal that renames what precedes it, and this one stands before the object of the very preposition written beside it, so dropping it diminishes that preposition's rendering and nothing else. Two limits. Where a connective morpheme stands in the clause and the ASV writes a bare *even* for it, rule 14 governs and the word is the connective's; the corpus aligns a waw to *even* in 179 units and to *even unto* in none, so read which of the two the ASV has written. And where the ASV leaves the preposition's own relation unstated, rule 40 governs as before and there is no expression to place. The corpus aligns a preposition to *even unto* in 33 units and `עַד` to *even to* in 28 more, always headed on the second word. And a marker on an object the ASV fronts before its clause and resumes inside it with a pronoun may be rendered *as for*: `וְאֶת־הַיְבוּסִי יוֹשְׁבֵי יְרוּשָׁלִַם לֹא־יָכְלוּ בְנֵי־יְהוּדָה לְהוֹרִישָׁם` → *And* ***as for*** *the Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out* gives *as for* to the marker, headed on *as* by rule 24, since the resuming *them* is the suffix's under rule 18 and nothing else answers to the two words. **The same limit governs that third family.** Where the ASV writes *as for* before a fronted phrase no marker stands on, no morpheme licenses the expression and it is its own `added` unit under rule 30, headed on *as*: `וּמַרְאֵיהֶם דְּמוּת אֶחָד לְאַרְבַּעְתָם` → *And* ***as for*** *their appearance, they four had one likeness* leaves the *as for* `added`, because `מַרְאֵיהֶם` is a bare noun and suffix with no marker and no preposition on it. Do not fold the expression into the fronted noun to avoid the `added`, for the reason just given about a surplus *even*, and do not reach for rule 33: that rule gives a supplied function word to a noun whose own case-function licenses it, and a topicalized nominal's fronting is not such a case-function. Where a morpheme does stand on the fronted phrase it takes the expression, whether that morpheme is a marker as above or a fronting `לְ` — `לָאוֹפַנִּים לָהֶם קוֹרָא` → ***As for*** *the wheels, they were called* gives *As for* to the `לְ` under rule 11. **And a marker on a direct object the ASV demotes to a role phrase takes the preposition written for it.** Where the ASV recasts the marked object as the role the thing serves and writes a supplied *for* or *as* before it, promoting the object's appositive to the English verb's object — `וְהֵבִיא אֵת־קָרְבָּנוֹ שְׂעִיר עִזִּים` → *he shall bring* ***for*** *his oblation a goat* — that word is the marker's and it heads on it, since the marked noun keeps its own English and nothing else in the clause answers for the preposition. Rule 33 is what governs the same clause written without a marker, and it says so in its own terms: a nominal with no preposition and no object marker on it takes the supplied word itself, as `וְהֵבִיא קָרְבָּנוֹ` → ***for*** *his oblation* and `יָבִיא קָרְבָּנוֹ` → ***as*** *his oblation* do. So read whether a marker stands on the noun before placing the word, and do not leave it `added`: one of the two morphemes always licenses it. Test by subtraction: drop the English word and ask which morpheme has lost its rendering. If nothing but the object relation is diminished, the marker takes the word; if the ASV writes the object bare — *he built the house* — the marker is `unrepresented`. Do not confuse H853 with its homograph the preposition `אֵת` *with* (H854), which is an ordinary preposition aligning by rule 11.
amendments.why: Rule 16's appositional-*even* sentence is written to catch any *even* standing before a phrase no marker marks, and it ends *whatever markers stand elsewhere in the clause* — which reaches, unintentionally, the *even* of an extent preposition's *even unto*. NUM.21 met that four times (21.24, 21.26, 21.30 twice) and every verse pass hedged it with 'the competing reading marks *even* added', which is the signal that the contract was underdetermined rather than that the edge was wrong. The evidence round settles it: 33 corpus units align a preposition to *even unto* headed on *unto*, 28 more align ad to *even to*, and no unit anywhere aligns a waw to *even unto*, so the pair is the preposition's rendering and never a connective's. The added paragraph qualifies the over-broad sentence where it stands rather than pointing back at it from a new rule, keeps rule 14's bare *even* for a waw (179 units) and rule 40's unrendered preposition out of its scope, and leaves every existing sentence of rule 16 intact.

conventions: An ad rendered *even unto* is one aligned unit on the preposition, headed on *unto*; the *even* is not `added` (21.24 s017, 21.26 s026, 21.30 s006 and s010). No waw and no object marker stands in any of those clauses to answer for the word, and the corpus aligns a preposition to *even unto* in 33 units and a waw to *even unto* in none. Where the ASV writes a bare *unto* instead, the preposition takes only that (21.24 s015, 21.30 s013).

derek plus a place name rendered *by the way of X* (21.1, 21.4, 21.33): the supplied *by* is the adverbial accusative's own under rule 33 and stays with derek, which keeps its English noun *way*, so rule 19's directional-construct rider does not reach it and the relation still goes to the rectum. The phrase's single *the* is then placed by rule 29 on the evidence of the rectum: fronted onto a present article the ASV renders anarthrously (21.1, 21.33), and supplied on the construct where the chain writes no article morpheme at all (21.4). Where the ASV instead spends its own noun on the construct — 21.22 *the king's highway* — rule 29's possessive case governs the *the*.

report: All three evidence requests were answered; nothing was left outstanding. The corpus aligns a preposition to *even unto* in 33 units headed on *unto* (30 of them on the lemma ad), ad to *even to* in 28 more, and a waw to *even unto* in none. That settles NUM.21.24 s017, 21.26 s026 and 21.30 s006/s010: the *even* is the preposition's own rendering and is not `added`, and no waw or object marker stands in any of those clauses to compete for it. The four verse passes had each hedged this the same way, so the chapter was already consistent — it was the hedge, not the edge, that needed answering.

Checked every candidate group printed in full. Each difference is licensed by the source or by the English the ASV wrote: ad renders as *unto* / *even unto* / *until* word for word; the apodosis waws of 21.8 and 21.9 are analysed identically in both verses (*and* / *when* / unrepresented); al-pene fuses headed on paneh at both 21.11 and 21.20, and li-qrat headed on qara at both 21.23 and 21.33; an explicit pronoun takes only its written English while the copula goes to the predicate at both 21.16 and 21.26 (rule 20); a directive he takes its own word at 21.16 and 21.23 while a bare place name takes the supplied one at 21.19, 21.27 and 21.33 (rules 32, 33).

The article work — the largest recurring judgment here — is internally consistent under rule 29. Fronting is used exactly where the ASV renders the rectum anarthrously (21.1 *the way of Atharim*, 21.9 *the serpent of brass*, 21.20 *the top of Pisgah*, 21.33 *the way of Bashan* and *the king of Bashan*); the arthrous count exactly where the ASV writes a *the* before the rectum's own word (21.3, 21.4, 21.13, 21.15, 21.18, 21.21, 21.25, 21.26, 21.31, 21.34); the possessive case at 21.22 *the king's highway*; and supplied *the*s only where no article morpheme is present (21.14, 21.24, 21.29). Demonstrative phrases follow rule 41's determiner count: where a demonstrative pronoun stands it takes the single written determiner and both articles go unrepresented (21.2, 21.17, 21.25), and where none stands the noun's own article takes the written *this* (21.5).

The four `added` units are consistent with each other and with rule 20: the italic supplied verbs *they journeyed* (21.16, 21.18) and *reacheth* (21.30) are lexical verbs for clauses whose Hebrew writes none, and the italic *and* at 21.18 coordinates two prepositional phrases with no conjunction morpheme between them (rule 14's last sentence). Nowhere does the chapter fold a comparable supply into a neighbouring morpheme, so the table's blindness to `added` units hides nothing here.

BSB disagreements: none is a genuine error. All 11 Td, all 8 To, the 5 R and the 4 C cases are the documented convention differences — rule 16 on the object marker, rule 29/47 on an article the ASV writes no determiner for, rule 27 on the le of lemor, rule 26 on the repeated second ben, rule 40 on a recast dative or on the be at 21.5 whose object the ASV promotes to a direct object, and rule 14 on an unrendered apodosis waw. The single Pp3fs case (21.26 hiw) is rule 22's resumptive pronoun the ASV does not separately render; the clause's *was* is the predicate's under rule 20, which is how 21.16 reads the same construction.

Recorded two conventions and left the other 68 repeated notes unlogged: they restate rules 14, 16, 18, 19, 29 and 44 and would only hide the two that matter. One amendment returned, to rule 16, whose appositional-*even* sentence is over-broad and would send a later reader to `added` for exactly the *even unto* this chapter met four times.
